properties.title: Tornado Warning issued October 21 at 5:19AM MST until October 21 at 5:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
TORFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 545 AM MST.

* At 519 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Garland Prairie, or 18 miles west of Flagstaff,
moving northeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Fort Valley, Parks, Bellemont, Garland Prairie, Government Prairie,
Maine, Camp Navajo, Whitehorse Lake, Scholz Lake, Wing Mountain,
Lava River Cave and Sycamore Falls.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 175 and 187. Highway 180 between
mile markers 223 and 227.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
White Horse Lake Campground and Camp Raymond.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Sycamore Falls, Lower Sycamore Falls "The Golden Pond" and Paradise
Forks.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Tornadoes are difficult to observe at night. Take cover now!

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 21 at 5:12AM MST until October 21 at 5:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 512 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles southwest of
Garland Prairie, or 22 miles northwest of Sedona, moving northeast at
40 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect damage
to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles.

Locations impacted include...
Williams, Red Lake, Parks, Bellemont, Garland Prairie, Sherwood
Forest Estates, Government Prairie, Maine, Camp Navajo, H A Clark
Memorial Field, Sycamore Canyon Wilderness, Whitehorse Lake, Bill
Williams Mountain, Scholz Lake, Sycamore Falls, Kaibab Lake, J.D.
Dam Lake and Wing Mountain.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 159 and 186. Business Interstate
40 between mile markers 163 and 165. State Route 64 between mile
markers 186 and 198.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
White Horse Lake Campground, Camp Raymond, Dogtown Lake Campground,
Kaibab Lake Campground and Bill Williams Campground.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Sycamore Falls, Lower Sycamore Falls "The Golden Pond" and Paradise
Forks.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing large hail.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 20 at 9:12PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end of this
week. There is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage
next week after northeasterly winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.5 feet early this
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 20 at 8:47PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...

Satilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Wednesday evening at 900 PM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Satilla River at Atkinson.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Warners Landing, Louis Landing and
secondary roads around KOA campgrounds begin to flood. At 14.0
feet, River Rock Road begins to experience flooding across the
road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 14.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 13.6 feet Friday
evening.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
